criterion: Real-time ambient occlusion (raw/renderer/ao_realtime.hpp): the GTAO integral of post_gtao at a frame budget, scored against the CPU reference raw::post::gtao at 16 slices by 16 steps.
written: 2026-11-18. The three bounds were fixed while the pass still ran 1 slice by 6 steps (it measured 0.012, 0.017 and 0.019 then). The defaults later moved to 2 slices by 16 steps and the bounds were kept.

pass.prefilter: depth -> half-resolution view depth, one pixel of each 2 x 2 block; with accumulation on the chosen pixel cycles through all four in four frames
pass.levels: three coarser levels, each texel the mean of the input texels within 10 % of the nearest one
pass.trace: half resolution, 2 slices of 16 steps a side by default. Slice turn and step offset come from a 64 x 64 blue-noise field (void and cluster, generated at start, src/renderer/ao_noise.cpp) moved each frame by a rank-1 sequence. Depth at a step is interpolated in 1 / depth from the four texels around the exact position, with the nearest texel alone where they span more than 10 %. A step reads the level whose texels are about half the step spacing.
pass.resolve: full resolution: depth-weighted upsample of the four half-resolution texels, a running mean along the motion vectors (a pixel's own trace weighs 1, a value borrowed from neighbours 0.15), history rejected where it is off screen or held another depth (10 %), a 4 x 4 depth-weighted mean while a pixel has under 7 frames of history, and the frame times the visibility as the second target

rhi_additions: TextureFormat::RG16Float (D3D12, Vulkan and WebGPU format tables) and sampled R32Float and RG16Float textures on D3D12. The pass is five raster passes over textures, so it needed no compute texture bindings.
check: tests/gpu/ao_realtime.cpp (ctest gpu_ao_realtime; CI runs it on WARP). Scene: a floor, a wall and a ball at 480 x 270, the game's projection terms, radius 35. Error: mean |visibility - reference| over the frame, a 16-pixel border left out, visibility clamped to 1.

controls_that_must_fail.radius_x2: the pass with twice the radius scores at least 1.5 times the converged error
controls_that_must_fail.zero_motion_vectors: the scene slides 3 pixels a frame for 24 frames; with zero motion vectors and depth rejection off, the error over the pixels the reference puts under 0.9 is at least 1.5 times the error with the right vectors

measured.adapters: RTX 4090 and WARP gave the same numbers to five decimals

blue_noise: tests/test_ao_noise.cpp: every rank once, deterministic for a seed, low-frequency ratio 0.14 against 0.96 for the same ranks shuffled (the white-noise control); bound 0.25.
game_content: On a captured 3840 x 2160 game frame the pass runs behind RAW's D3D12 bridge; cost and error at each step are in RAW's docs/D3D12_BRIDGE.md and its evidence folder. There the 16 x 16 reference is itself 0.062 from a 48 x 48 one, and the pass at its defaults is 0.050 from the first and 0.060 from the second.
limits: The slide is synthesised: each frame shows the same buffers moved sideways, so no surface is uncovered and the view rays of the moved content are not those of a real camera pan. The noise is blue in space and a rank-1 sequence in time at a fixed pixel; along a motion path the sequence a surface sees is no longer low-discrepancy. Past half of the ranks the generator keeps filling voids where the paper swaps roles. D3D12 only: the shaders are hand-written HLSL. The motion vector has no depth component, so a camera moving fast along its axis can trip the depth rejection.
